title: EFC — How Energy Flow Sustains Spacetime
description: Proposes Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), the hypothesis that a globally conserved yet locally dynamic energy flow—modulated by entropy and matter distribution—acts as the scaffolding that sustains and shapes spacetime curvature. The paper outlines a research program to relate energy-flow and entropy gradients to observed gravitational phenomena across scales and calls for simulations and comparisons to gravitational lensing and CMB data. Its contribution is a conceptual framework and test agenda rather than new empirical results.

key_results.main_finding: Articulates the hypothesis that global energy flow, locally modulated by entropy and matter distribution, sustains and shapes spacetime curvature across scales.

kill_criteria: KC1: Cross-scale analyses (from black-hole environments to cosmic voids) show no correlation between measured local energy flux or entropy gradients and spacetime curvature once mass–energy density (GR stress–energy) is controlled for, within observational uncertainties.

KC2: Gravitational lensing maps and CMB anisotropies are fully accounted for by standard GR+ΛCDM with no systematic residuals attributable to an energy-flow or entropy-gradient term across the tested scales.
KC3: Simulations that implement the proposed energy-flow scaffolding fail to improve or match fits to observed large-scale structure, lensing, or expansion history compared to baseline GR+ΛCDM.

KC4: Operational definitions or proxies for "energy flow" and associated entropy gradients cannot be made consistent with conservation laws or yield non-reproducible measurements across independent instruments and surveys.
